criteria.criterion: crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs has a new pub fn check_code_survey, called from check_reading_acceptance. Its doc comment names the root cause: the reading stage designs storage, override and test seams from a general idea of the feature without surveying what the records validation accepts or where resolution and probing happen in the code. It cites jobs 20261028-055601-hg0n and 20261028-082151-67fa and introspections 20261028-055651-dhh0 and 20261028-082240-77as.
criteria.evidence: Read in the diff: `pub fn check_code_survey(reading: &Reading) -> Result<()>` exists, and `check_reading_acceptance` calls `check_code_survey(reading)?;` between check_criteria_evidence and check_governance_coverage. The doc comment says: "the reading stage designs storage, override and test seams from a general idea of the feature, without surveying what the records validation accepts or where resolution and probing happen in the code." It cites jobs 20261028-055601-hg0n and 20261028-082151-67fa and introspections 20261028-055651-dhh0 and 20261028-082240-77as.

criteria.criterion: The change refuses more readings: change readings of class code or tests with a behavior criterion and no 'Code survey:' assumption naming a crates/ path are refused, and a higher refusal rate is intended. The CHANGELOG.md entry and the doc comment of check_code_survey say so, so the replay gate treats the rise as intended.
criteria.evidence: The doc comment says: "This check refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended." The CHANGELOG says: "This change refuses more readings, and the higher refusal rate is intended". The test code_survey_refusal_is_declared_intended asserts that criteria_intend_higher_refusal is true for the criterion text, checks the doc comment and CHANGELOG through include_str!, and shows the refusal happens. It passed. The brief's replay section reports 40 of 50 newly refused readings and says the job is not held because the criteria state the higher refusal rate is intended; that replay result is from Athena's run, not from this snapshot.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: a new unit test calls check_reading_acceptance with a reading of capability change, class_of_work code and one behavior criterion but no assumption starting 'Code survey:' naming a crates/ path. It is refused with an error naming the missing survey. The same reading with such an assumption is accepted. The test fails if the check_reading_acceptance call to check_code_survey is removed.
criteria.evidence: code_survey_missing_is_refused_and_present_is_accepted builds a code reading with one Behavior criterion. It calls check_reading_acceptance through accept(), calls unwrap_err, and asserts the error contains "`Code survey:`", "crates/" and "was refused". The same reading with a survey is accepted. It passed, along with code_survey_tests_class_is_refused_too and code_survey_must_start_with_the_label_and_name_a_crates_path. If the call were removed, the reading would be accepted and unwrap_err would panic, so the test would fail. I confirmed this by reading the test, not by removing the call.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: a unit test shows that a reading with a create deliverable for a record or data file under crates/ is refused unless the survey names check_record_file, AnyRecord, or a named round-trip test function or path. A survey that only mentions 'allow-list' in passing is refused. A criterion that mentions records/ only to exclude it does not trigger the requirement. Docs-only readings, readings with no capability and readings with only content criteria are still accepted, and the existing reading tests pass unchanged.
criteria.evidence: These tests passed: code_survey_new_record_file_needs_named_evidence ("allow-list" alone and "round-trip" in prose are refused; check_record_file, AnyRecord, records_round_trip_every_kind and a round-trip.rs path are accepted), code_survey_record_file_requirement_ignores_ordinary_deliverables_and_criteria (a criterion saying 'records/ is not changed' is accepted), and code_survey_does_not_apply_outside_its_gate (docs, decline, question and content-only readings are accepted). The diff adds tests and edits no existing one. The recorded `cargo test --locked` passed (1577 tests).

findings.summary: The record-or-data-file rule fires on any newly created .toml, .json, .yaml or .csv file under crates/ (Cargo.toml excepted), such as a rustfmt.toml or a test fixture JSON file. Those readings must then name record evidence they do not need.
findings.evidence: is_record_or_data_deliverable treats any Create under crates/ with one of those extensions as a record file. Narrower alternative: limit the rule to files that the records validation (check_record_file) actually reads, or to the directories it covers. The error message is clear, so a refused reader can recover, and the reading asked for this rule ("a create deliverable for a record or data file under crates/").

findings.summary: The required survey is only a label plus a crates/ path, so a reader can satisfy it without surveying anything. This is the mechanism the reading specified, so it is noted rather than counted against the change.
findings.evidence: check_code_survey accepts any assumption that starts with 'Code survey:' and contains 'crates/' followed by an alphanumeric character. It does not check that the path exists or that it relates to the deliverables.

findings.summary: Criterion 3's claim that the test fails without the call was checked by reading the test, not by removing the call.
findings.evidence: The test calls unwrap_err on accept(code_reading(&[], ...)). Only check_code_survey produces that refusal, so without the call the reading would be accepted and the test would fail. The verifier may not modify code, so this was not run.

summary: I find that the change does what the retry asked. It adds `check_code_survey` to crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs and calls it from `check_reading_acceptance`. The check refuses a reading that changes code or tests, has a behavior criterion, and has no assumption that starts `Code survey:` and names a crates/ path. If the reading also creates a record or data file under crates/, or changes a records.rs, the survey must name check_record_file, AnyRecord or a round-trip test; mentioning "allow-list" in passing does not count. The doc comment and the CHANGELOG entry give the root cause, both job IDs and both introspection IDs. Both also say the higher refusal rate is intended, which the replay recognised: 40 of 50 replayed readings are newly refused, and the job was not held. The reader brief gains a rule line and a guide paragraph (`CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE`) covering everything criterion 5 asks for. I ran three things in this snapshot, and all passed: the 7 new code_survey tests (`cargo test --locked -p athena-core code_survey`), the reader brief tests, and all 84 athena-context tests. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and full test runs also passed. Only the three files on the deliverables list changed, and no existing tests were edited. My two minor findings: the record-file rule treats any newly created .toml or .json file under crates/ as a data file, and no test actually removes the call to prove it is needed; that criterion part was checked by reading the test.
